files.title: Your subcontractor agreement — read it on your phone, sign on the screen, keep the PDF
files.summary: The Independent Contractor Agreement between ENLVN Pty Ltd (Paint Group) and your business lives in the portal. Your trading name, ABN and address are already filled in from your profile. Read it through, tick, sign with your finger and tap Sign; a PDF copy with Paint Group's countersignature is emailed to you and kept under Profile → Subcontractor agreement, where you can download it any time. Job offers wait until it is signed. It runs for twelve months; a month before it ends the portal asks you to sign the new term. If you signed on paper before the portal, the office uploads that copy and you are not asked again.

files.title: Subcontractor agreements on PC Command — the queue items and the Contractors tag
files.summary: PC Command carries two work items from the one queue — Agreement not signed (an active contractor with no signed, unexpired agreement: a new one whose offers wait, an existing one asked or not yet asked, or an expired one) and Agreement expiring (inside the 30-day renewal window). Both link to the contractor's record where the office taps Request signature or uploads a paper copy. PC Command → Contractors shows the Agreement not signed tag on the same rows. A job offer to a contractor without a current agreement refuses with agreement_unsigned or agreement_expired.

files.title: Subcontractor agreements — who has signed, Request signature, upload a paper copy
files.summary: Contractors sign the Independent Contractor Agreement in the portal with their details filled in; the countersigned PDF is on their record under Documents and the office gets a copy by email. Contractors shows an Agreement line per contractor (Signed v1 · date, Uploaded · date, Not signed, Expires …) with Request signature; the contractor record has the same plus Download signed copy and Add signed agreement for contractors who signed on paper. Job offers refuse (error agreement_unsigned or agreement_expired) until a signed, unexpired agreement is on file. Everyone on the books before the feature keeps their offers until you tap Request signature, which starts a grace window (14 days, Settings → agreement_rules.graceDays) before offers stop.

files.title: Control every automatic message from one screen
files.summary: Settings → Automations — switch any message on or off, choose Text, Email or Both, decide whether the office approves it first, set sending hours and the daily limit, and edit the wording with a live preview and a test send.

files.title: A call back — what is wrong, when to go back, and marking it fixed
files.summary: When a job needs a return visit to fix workmanship, the office logs a call back. It shows on Home and on the job with what is wrong, the photos and the day of the return visit. You mark it fixed with a photo; the office confirms and closes it.

files.title: A call back — what is wrong, when to go back, and marking it fixed
files.summary: When a job needs a return visit to fix workmanship, the office logs a call back. It shows on Home and on the job with what is wrong, the photos and the day of the return visit. You mark it fixed with a photo; the office confirms and closes it.

files.title: Log a call back, book the return visit and close it
files.summary: A call back is a return visit on another day to fix workmanship. One record, four ways in — a failed quality check, a flagged walk-through, the customer ringing, or a visit ticked as a call back on the schedule board — each with a reason and the date it was reported. It pauses the customer's invoice chasing until you close it, counts against the painter who did the job, never reopens a closed job and never touches the painter's pay.

files.title: Contacts — every customer in one list, and how a contact gets onto an estimate
files.summary: The Contacts list holds every CRM customer and every person ever used on an estimate; the list and the estimate's Contact card each have a search bar to find them, and whatever you put on an estimate is saved to the list by itself.

files.title: Join from your invitation, and keep your mobile on file
files.summary: What the invitation link asks for (your name, a mobile and a password), why your mobile is required, and how to change it on your profile.

files.title: Invite a painter, open their record, and remove one who should never have been there
files.summary: How the office invites a contractor or employed painter, what each painter's own page shows (mobile, crew, paperwork, every job and their quality-check record), how to add or fix their mobile, how to reveal their bank details, how the quality-check setting works, and when a painter can be removed rather than suspended.

files.title: Your first hour in the CRM
files.summary: The four tabs, what Today is asking you to do, how to find any customer in two keystrokes, how to log a call or book a visit, and how to switch between dark and light.

files.title: Your account — Home, Payments, Messages and My colours on a phone
files.summary: What each tab of your Paint Group account shows and how to use it — the grouped estimate list and address chips on Home, the three numbers and PDF buttons on Payments, the message threads with their unread badge, and your colours listed by colour with a By area view.

files.title: The home dashboard for a project coordinator — jobs, painters, and what needs you today
files.summary: /home for a PC login: the needs-doing strip with the console's job cards, PC Command (right-now job counts that each open their list), Contractors (on-time, silent, QA first time, hours vs estimate with the entered/schedule coverage) and the job-side Activity feed — never margin, P&L, targets or marketing.

files.title: The home dashboard — what you land on, what each tile means, and the numbers the office types in
files.summary: /home is where every staff login lands — a needs-doing strip, then the sections for your roles as tiles you can press for the rows behind them, an i for what each counts, and Export CSV; roles are ticked on Settings → Staff logins, and the Dashboard folder in Settings holds the target, marketing spend and thresholds (owner/admin only).

files.title: 12 Demo Street — your practice job
files.summary: A practice job on your own account for the induction. It uses the same screens as a real job, nothing in it is real, and nothing you do in it counts toward your status light or your money. Start it from the Jobs tab, find it under the Demo heading, and reset it any time to go back to the start.

files.title: 12 Demo Street — a painter's practice job, and why it is in none of your numbers
files.summary: Every contractor can have one practice job for the induction. It is a real work order on their account, rendered by the same screens, but it is left out of PC Command, the schedule, the Contractors strip, Payments, the dashboard, every sweep and Google Calendar. You can open it from its link and reset it for the painter.

files.title: Set up or reset a contractor's practice job from their record
files.summary: On a contractor's record under Contractors there is a Demo property line. Set up demo gives them 12 Demo Street for the induction; Reset demo puts it back to the start. It never appears in their job list, their offers count, or anywhere money or status is counted.

files.title: Chat with us from your estimate — ask anything, and we reply in the same place
files.summary: Ask a question at the top, Chat with us in the bottom bar or Message us at the bottom all open one chat box in the corner of your estimate; your message reaches our office straight away, we reply there and let you know by text and email, and outside office hours the box tells you when we'll be back.

files.title: A customer's chat message reaches you in the corner of every staff page — and by email and text
files.summary: A message sent from the chat on a customer's estimate becomes a Waiting row in the chat dock on every staff page, emails and texts the staff routed for "Customer chat message", or the office address when nobody is; reply from the dock, the builder's Messages or by answering the alert email, and the customer is texted and emailed the reply.

files.title: A price for an office, warehouse, shop or building — online where we can, a quick visit where we can't
files.summary: Pick the kind of space; offices, warehouses, retail, aged care, clinics and schools get a guide range that an estimator confirms; strata, shop fronts, hospitals and any outside work get a short brief and a booked visit instead.

files.title: Get a painting price online, in about two minutes
files.summary: A few quick screens give you a guide range; then you can tighten it room by room or side by side, and send it to your estimator to fix the price — or book a visit at any point.

files.title: Online estimates from the office side — the queue, the pack, and the three things you can do with a request
files.summary: Every online quote lands in Waiting on you with a promise clock; the Pack tab shows what the customer built and what they assumed; you fix the price, ask a question or book a visit from the strip, and the measured tree goes to the property when you fix.

files.title: Quoting from your trade account — saved specs, the spec sheet, and quoting again from the file
files.summary: An agency or building manager quotes in a few taps: pick the property, pick a saved spec, open the sheet, send it for confirmation; a property your estimator has measured is never measured again, and a tenant can send photos from a link.

files.title: Find help inside the portal
files.summary: Where the guides live in the portal, how to read one with its pictures and short film, how to search for the thing you are stuck on, and how to replay the "show me around" tour from your first sign-in.

files.title: Find help inside the office console
files.summary: Where the office and project-coordinator guides live, how to open one with its pictures and film, how to search across them, and what the painters see in their own Help tab.

files.title: See your earlier quotes and jobs in your account
files.summary: If Paint Group quoted or painted for you before this website existed, those quotes and jobs appear in your account as records once you sign in with your email.

files.title: Read a customer's history from Airtable, and pick up a job that was signed in PaintScout
files.summary: What the Airtable import put on each customer record, why an imported estimate opens as a card instead of the builder, how to find imported history on the Estimates list, and how the 35 signed PaintScout jobs sit in the Unscheduled tray ready to offer.

files.title: Your induction — choose your language, read each module in it, tick it
files.summary: Pick the language you read best on the first screen of the induction (English, Dari, Farsi, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese or Italian, as Paint Group switches them on). Everything you read and tick to confirm — the thirteen modules and the six finish standards sections — is then in that language; the app, the slides and the practice job stay in English. One tick per module, resumable; the last tick completes the induction and emails you a PDF of everything you ticked. Job offers start when the induction is complete, your facilitator has passed the practical check, and your public liability insurance is on file. Existing contractors do the shorter refresher with no practical check; a worker login does the worker version and can be put on a job once it is complete and checked.

files.title: Induction — languages, who has ticked what, the practical check, the gates
files.summary: Painters read and tick the induction and the six finish standards sections in the language they choose. Settings → Communications → Induction languages switches a language on once its wording has been tested. A contractor's record shows their induction — full or refresher, modules ticked, completion, the practical check you record task by task, and whether offers are allowed. New painters get no job offer until the induction is complete, the five-task check is passed and insurance is verified; existing painters are invited to the refresher with a grace period; a worker login cannot be put on a real job until their worker induction and three-task check are in. The wording lives in translation files loaded by the seed script, never typed into Settings.

files.title: Pay an invoice — press Pay for the amount, our bank details and the reference to use
files.summary: What happens when you press Pay on an invoice from Paint Group: a box with the amount due, the bank transfer details and the invoice number to use as the reference, plus a card option when it is offered.

files.title: Payments — collect from customers, pay contractors and suppliers, and see each job's profit
files.summary: The one Payments page (Payments in the sidebar): the headline and four blocks, chasing customers by job, one-press Paid with Undo, cash, sending with a due date, the deposit size, messages, the job panel with Money in and Money out and profit, contractor invoices (approve, pay with a reference, Green fast terms and holds, RCTIs, expenses and ask-first requests), supplier invoices (confirm, record as any cost, no job yet), Activity, card payments, what the customer sees when they press Pay, and when an invoice turns overdue.

files.title: The live-updates demo on your estimate — an example of the updates you'll get while we paint
files.summary: Under "A few extra details" on your estimate, a glowing card opens a phone playing an example of the day-by-day updates you will receive if you go ahead, shown with your address, your rooms and your own photos; the days, times and painter are examples, not your schedule.

files.title: The live-updates demo card on a customer's estimate — when it shows, what it says, and the one setting behind it
files.summary: An estimate with a presentation attached carries one glowing card in the presentation's capability panel ("A few extra details"); pressed, it opens a phone playing an example of the day-by-day updates the customer will get, built from their own address, rooms and photos; trade accounts see commercial wording; the Demo painter comes from Settings → Website.

files.title: Locked out? Get back into your portal
files.summary: What to do when you cannot sign in — ask the office for a reset link or a new password, what the emailed link does, and how to choose your new password.

files.title: Sign in to your account with an emailed link or code
files.summary: How to get into your Paint Group account without a password — ask for a sign-in link, open it and press Open my account, or type the code from the same email — and what to do if a link says it has expired.

files.title: Change a password or send a reset link, for staff and for painters
files.summary: Where the master user sets a staff login's password by hand or emails a reset link, where any staff member does the same for a painter from the painter's page, what the reset link does when it is clicked, and why a removed staff login can be created again with the same address.

files.title: Approve, change or skip an automatic message before it goes
files.summary: CRM → Messages to approve — the automatic job messages the office chose to approve first, and anything held for sending hours or the daily limit. Approve, edit then send, or skip.

files.title: Your pickups and drop-offs — where the paint is, when it comes, what to bring back
files.summary: The office plans how paint, materials, gear and rubbish get to and from your job. You see it in two places — a "Your pickups and drop-offs today" card on your home screen and a "Getting it to site" section on the job sheet — with the shop's address and phone, the order reference to quote at the counter, and a tick for each pickup, drop-off or return that is yours.

files.title: Plan the week's paint, materials, gear and rubbish on the Movements board
files.summary: How the Movements tab works — the tray of chips built from the jobs, the lanes for the supplier, each painter and each staff member, dragging a chip onto a day (or an hour), the chip sheet for the shop, time, order reference and note, Ordered ✓, Nearby and While-you're-there suggestions, the Sources view that shows one materials list in its three places, the Day run plans, the Map with one icon per job and the drag-to-order card, and the Gear register.

files.title: Paint Home — pricing your home online
files.summary: Paint Home is for apartments, units, townhouses and smaller homes; you type your address, answer a few questions, see a price range in about ten minutes, and one short call confirms it. The painters, the guarantee and the insurance are the same ones behind Paint Group, which powers Paint Home.

files.title: Paint Home — the second shopfront: its words, its cards, and Settings → Brands
files.summary: Paint Home (painthome.com.au) is the same business, wizard, painters, CRM and invoicing under a second name; its words are edited on the Paint Home tab of Website copy, its three cards are home jobs under the phone-close price with their own featured rank, and Settings → Brands holds each shopfront's domain, phone, legal line and accent colour.

files.title: Read and answer messages from the office about a job — with photos
files.summary: Messages from the office land in Messages on your Home screen, one line per job (job number and suburb), and on that job's page, where you can reply with text and photos from your phone.

files.title: Read and answer messages from the office about a job — with photos
files.summary: Messages from the office about a job you are on land in Messages on your Home screen (job number and suburb) and on the job's page, where you can reply with text and photos from your phone.

files.title: Message a painter about a job, with photos, from the job page
files.summary: The Messages box on a job in PC Command — one conversation per painter on the job, text and photos both ways, a line under each of your messages saying whether the painter was texted, and a card on PC Command when a painter writes back that clears once you read it.

files.title: Your status — the traffic light, what it gets you, and how to reach Green
files.summary: Home shows a traffic light with your status in words. Tap it for My status — why you are on that colour, the three measures as plain counts, your last 10 jobs, what to do next and how the colours work. Reward only, never a deduction.

files.title: Your status as a lead painter — the traffic light on the jobs you led
files.summary: A lead painter sees the traffic light on Home and My status, scored on the jobs they led. It reads "jobs you led" and never mentions priority jobs or fast payment. A painter who has not led a job sees no status at all.

files.title: Contractors in PC Command — every painter's light, call backs, rewards and who has signed
files.summary: The Contractors tab in PC Command counts painters by colour, open call backs, rewards due and standards not signed, and lists one row per painter with their light, checks, app updates, call backs, streak and trend. Tap a row for their last 10 jobs, the bonus history, a Spot check or to log a call back.

files.title: Request more materials, mark a rained-off day, add your certificates later
files.summary: From a job you can ask the office for more materials (what and how much) and see their reply on the same card; you can tell the office there was no work today (rained off, site not ready, sick) and once they confirm, that day's update reminders are not counted. During induction you can say "I will add this later" on your public liability certificate and carry on — you are texted a reminder on days 2, 4 and 6, and job offers start once it is in.

files.title: Materials requests, no-work days and missing certificates on PC Command
files.summary: Three cards painters raise from their phone land on PC Command. Materials — order it and reply on the job (the reply shows on the painter's phone). No work today — confirm and that day's update reminders are not counted, or decline. Insurance — a contractor with no verified certificate, with how many reminder texts they have had; no job offers until it is in.

files.title: Switching the portal between dark and light
files.summary: The round button at the top of every portal screen swaps the whole portal between the dark look and a light one — useful in bright sun or on a site where the dark screen is hard to read. Your choice sticks on that phone until you change it back.

files.title: Switching the painter portal between dark and light
files.summary: The round button at the top of every portal screen swaps the whole portal between the dark look and a light one — useful in bright sun or on a site where the dark screen is hard to read. Your choice sticks on that phone until you change it back.

files.title: Answer a job offer and manage your booked dates
files.summary: How a job offer reaches you in the portal, what the 24-hour clock means, how to accept, propose a different start date or decline, and how to ask to move a job you have already accepted.

files.title: Your assigned jobs — accepting one, your calendar, and what to do if you can't make a day
files.summary: How a job reaches you as an employed painter — it lands in your calendar already booked, you tap Accept once to say you've seen it, several of you can share one job with one lead painter, and you can flag days you can't make.

files.title: Offer a job to a painter and manage the booking on the scheduling board
files.summary: How the Schedule tab works — drag an accepted job onto a contractor's row to send a 24-hour offer, or onto an employed painter's row to assign it (several painters, one lead), handle proposals and reschedule requests, cancel or move a booking, and what the customer receives.

files.title: Invoice Paint Group for a job
files.summary: How your invoices are drafted for you in the portal, how to send a progress claim at any time, how to check and submit the sign-off invoice, and how to see when it has been approved and paid.

files.title: Claim an expense you paid for on a job
files.summary: The Expenses tab for employed painters — a receipt photo, the category, the amount from the receipt, which job, and who paid; what happens over $100; and how a claim you paid yourself gets paid back.

files.title: Approve and pay contractor invoices on Payments → Contractors
files.summary: What the office sees when a contractor submits an invoice or progress claim, how the figures are drafted and reconciled to the job, and how Approve, Paid (with the bank reference and date) and the remittance work on Payments → Contractors.

files.title: Read the finish standards, and open the one for the surface you are painting
files.summary: The Paint Group finish standards for Levels 2, 3 and 4 live under Help — a grid of interior and exterior surfaces, each with what we expect at every level, plus the rules for every job, your time and variations, the defect rule, the final checklist and the words we use. Every work order has one "What we expect on this job" drop-down at the top with the standards for that job's level.

files.title: Read the finish standards, and open the one for the surface you are painting
files.summary: The Paint Group finish standards for Levels 2, 3 and 4 live under Help — a grid of interior and exterior surfaces, each with what we expect at every level, plus the rules for every job, extra time, the defect rule, the final checklist and the words we use. Every job sheet has one "What we expect on this job" drop-down at the top with the standards for that job's level.

files.title: Judge a quality check against the finish standards the painter was given
files.summary: The finish standards (Levels 2, 3 and 4) are data under PC Command → Standards, and every job carries one "What we expect on this job" drop-down with each surface's standard at that job's level — the same record the painter opens from their work order, so both of you judge against the same words. Also covers the small-job hours setting and how the standards are loaded.

files.title: Invite someone to your organisation's workspace
files.summary: An admin of a trade organisation adds a person under Team by email and access level; someone new is emailed a link to choose a password, someone with a login already is emailed a link that opens the workspace.

files.title: Your hours — logged for you, plus any extra you work
files.summary: How an employed painter's hours reach payroll — a standard day is logged automatically on every day you are on a job, you add only extra hours, Start day / Finish day is for a day with two jobs, and what the status words mean.

files.title: Employed painters' days — logged and approved automatically, plus time off and the payroll CSV
files.summary: The Timesheets tab in PC Command — the standard day that logs itself every evening and approves itself, the one kind of day that still waits (no cost rate), days that need a manual entry, painters' extra hours, leave and RDO requests, recording a day by hand, the allocated-vs-actual table, the payroll CSV, and where the cost rate lives.

files.title: Create a trade login or give an existing customer the trade workspace
files.summary: Settings → Trade accounts makes a trade organisation from an email and a starting password, or flips an existing customer to trade; a new trade account is matched by its email only, never by phone.

files.title: Training videos — short films showing the painter portal
files.summary: Every training video in one place for painters — one short film per job, each opening on YouTube in its own tab.

files.title: Training videos — short films showing the painter portal
files.summary: Every training video in one place for painters — one short film per job, each opening on YouTube in its own tab.

files.title: Training videos — short films that show the platform in use
files.summary: Every training video in one place for the office — one short film per job, each opening on YouTube in its own tab.

files.title: What happens when a customer books a site visit online
files.summary: A customer who has seen their guide price books a site visit themselves — they pick a time in their zone, confirm with a text code, and the visit lands on the Diary with its zone frozen. This explains what you see and what to do if something looks wrong.

files.title: Answer a request for a visit, a time or a call
files.summary: Customers who cannot book a slot themselves — pre-arranged areas, a suburb we don't know, nothing that suits, or a visit asked for before the price — send a request. It lands on CRM Today, due within one working day. You answer it by offering a time, which books the visit and tells the customer, or by marking it answered.

files.title: Set each estimator's week of site-visit slots, and the booking rules behind the calendar
files.summary: Settings → Visit schedule is each estimator's week — the slots, which zones can book each one, and the Friday 12:30 rule. Settings → Booking rules holds the numbers the calendar follows, the public holidays and the far-edge pairs.

files.title: Decide which suburbs can book a site visit, and in which zone
files.summary: Settings → Visit zones is the list of every Victorian suburb with its status — a bookable zone, pre-arranged, or out of area — the far-edge tick, who covers each zone, and a box to check what a customer at any address would be offered.

files.title: Your two-year workmanship warranty — what it covers, how long it lasts and how to make a claim
files.summary: Every job Paint Group completes is covered for two years from the day you sign off; this explains what is covered, what is not, where to find your certificate and how to report something that does not look right.

files.title: What the two-year workmanship warranty promises, where the customer sees it, and what you can and cannot change
files.summary: The warranty is approved, applies to every job for two years from sign-off, does not transfer to a new owner, and now appears on the customer's estimate as well as in their account — there is no switch to turn it off for a particular job.

files.title: Run a job from the first tick to the customer's signature
files.summary: How a booked job works on your phone in four steps — before photos in one batch, ticking surfaces off, after photos of every room or side, and finishing — plus raising a variation, the quality check, and handing the phone to the customer to sign off.

files.title: Your project, day by day — following the job and the photos your painting team sends
files.summary: Where to see each update from your painting team with the photos the office attached to it, where every area is up to, who is at your home, and what to do if a photo or update is missing.

files.title: Run a job from the first tick to the customer's signature
files.summary: How an assigned job works on your phone as an employed painter — the pre-start list, before photos in one batch, ticking surfaces off, after photos of every room or side, the finishing-up list, the quality check and the walkthrough — the same as every painter, with no money on it.

files.title: Run jobs through the seven lanes from the PC console
files.summary: The project coordinator's console — the attention queue and what its colours mean, the seven lanes, the pre-start list, pricing and releasing variations, approving drafted customer updates, quality checks, the walkthrough and sign-off gates, and closing.

files.title: Your crew — give each worker their own login, share jobs with them
files.summary: Add a worker by name and mobile and they get their own login by text. Share a job with them and they see the scope, the finish standard and the tick list on their own phone, and tick and photograph under their own name. They never see your price, offers, invoices, variations or messages. Remove a worker and their login stops opening your jobs at once.

files.title: Worker logins — who is on a contractor's crew and what they can see
files.summary: A contractor adds workers under Your crew; each gets a login by text and sees only the jobs shared with them — scope, standards, photos and ticks, never money. The contractor's record shows their crew, the induction state and how many jobs each worker sees. Ticks by a worker count for the contractor's job and carry the worker's name.

tours.title: Show me around
tours.summary: The first-sign-in tour of the contractor portal — one card per tab, Next, Back, Skip.
